s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic rash with erythematous annular plaques and perivascular inflammation
salient_findings: Erythematous annular plaques without scale on arms and legs
Superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils on biopsy
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 70s
Patient has recurrent primary peritoneal carcinoma
Patient is receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab
Rash started as an erythematous papule on right arm 2 months after initiation of new immunotherapy regimen
Rash gradually enlarged and spread to involve both legs
Patient denied any new systemic symptoms associated with onset of the rash
Oral terbinafine trial yielded no improvement
Biopsy from right arm showed superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils
PAS stain was negative for fungal organisms

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Numerous eosinophils on biopsy and pruritic rash

shortlist.label: Pembrolizumab-induced rash
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is receiving pembrolizumab and developed rash after initiation of therapy

shortlist.label: Ipilimumab-induced rash
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is receiving ipilimumab and developed rash after initiation of therapy

shortlist.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
shortlist.why_kept: Erythematous annular plaques on skin and perivascular inflammation on biopsy

shortlist.label: Well syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Eosinophilic infiltration and pruritic rash, consistent with Well syndrome

raw.rationale: The presence of numerous eosinophils in the biopsy and the clinical presentation of erythematous annular plaques without scale are consistent with eosinophilic cellulitis, which is a known side effect of immunotherapy

rejected.label: Pembrolizumab-induced rash
rejected.why: While pembrolizumab can cause a rash, the specific findings of eosinophilic cellulitis are more distinctive and explanatory

rejected.label: Ipilimumab-induced rash
rejected.why: Similar to pembrolizumab, ipilimumab can cause a rash, but the biopsy findings point more specifically to eosinophilic cellulitis

rejected.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
rejected.why: This condition can present with similar annular plaques, but the biopsy findings of eosinophilic cellulitis are more distinctive

rejected.label: Well syndrome
rejected.why: Well syndrome is a rare condition characterized by eosinophilia and cellulitis, but the clinical context and biopsy findings in this case are more consistent with eosinophilic cellulitis as a side effect of immunotherapy
